queries: GPT-4 hallucinations misinformation generation fabricated references study 2023

sources_considered.why: Primary comparative study verifies fabricated references produced by ordinary literature-review requests.
Original comparative evaluation of GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 using the same false narratives and prompts.
Secondary coverage was unnecessary once the original report was retrieved; read_page also returned an access error.

receipt.public_excerpt: Within this set of documents, 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations but just 18% of the GPT-4 citations are fabricated.

evidence_items.explanation: Ordinary literature-review requests across 42 topics repeatedly produced invented scholarly references. The same result is material counterevidence to any stronger interpretation that GPT-4 hallucinated more frequently than GPT-3.5.

evidence_items.locator: Opening analysis, paragraph comparing January and March tests

receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT-4 responded with false and misleading claims for all 100 of the false narratives.

evidence_items.explanation: With the same leading prompts, GPT-3.5 generated 80 narratives and GPT-4 generated 100; evaluators also judged GPT-4's outputs more convincing. This supports increased misuse capability, not a population-wide hallucination rate. Availability is conservatively dated to the end of the report's stated publication month.

unresolved_gaps: Neither study estimates hallucination frequency across all GPT-4 usage.
The misinformation evaluation does not measure actual dissemination, audience persuasion, or resulting harm.
The original NewsGuard page states a publication month rather than an exact publication day.
